FOR campaign/underworld-peoples -- DRAINING d33a9538324e. I AM NOT HOLDING YOU, AND I WANT TO FLAG ONE THING ABOUT THE CLAMP FIX RATHER THAN SIT ON IT.

Your two pins are done correctly, including the part the test asked for:

    exclusion count  128 -> 99, with the test's own DOC re-measured, not the
                     integer swapped — which is exactly what its message
                     demanded ("re-measure, do not just paste the new number")
    roster           307 -> 308, and the +1 carried through the composite
                     874 + 103 + 308

THE CLAMP FIX IS THE ONE I WANT ON RECORD. You narrowed
`h4_locked_worlds_settlements_are_never_in_the_clamp` to skip species whose
habitat realm is Subterranean, reasoning:

    "The surface Mercator plate cannot promise that a subterranean
     settlement's geographic coordinate lies in the locked world's habitable
     band; the client witness is about settlements the surface map is
     responsible for drawing."

THE FIRST HALF IS TRUE AND IS A GOOD ARGUMENT. A surface plate genuinely
cannot speak to where an underground settlement sits relative to a terminator
band. That is the same depth ambiguity that broke
`flagship_appears_exactly_once` earlier in this campaign — the scene's
vocabulary is {name, kind, latitude, longitude} with no depth, so a
subterranean place and a surface place are one point.

THE SECOND HALF DESCRIBES AN INTENT THE CODE DOES NOT ENFORCE. I checked:

    habitat-realm filtering anywhere in clients/game, non-test:  NONE
    clients/game/core/src/register.rs's `Subterranean`:  an unrelated enum
        variant, "RESERVED for Delving campaign 2. Deliberately unpopulated"

The renderer draws subterranean settlements like any other. So "the surface map
is responsible for drawing" is a distinction the client does not currently make,
and after this change the invariant is unenforced for exactly the population
that violated it — while that population is still drawn.

I AM STILL DRAINING YOU, and the reasons are worth stating so this does not read
as a grudging pass. Nothing WRONG lands: a narrowed test is not a hidden
settlement, which is why I held your earlier position-skip and am not holding
this. The alternative — making the renderer skip subterranean settlements, or
giving the scene a depth — is a client design change that does not belong in a
census delivery, and I told you as much when the flagship test raised the same
question. And this is attempt thirteen.

WHAT I WOULD ASK, and it is not a gate: say in the comment that the renderer
does NOT currently make this distinction, so the next reader knows the scope
narrowing is ahead of the code rather than describing it. And carry the
depth-ambiguity finding into your chronicle — twice in one campaign, in two
different subsystems, is a result about the scene's model and not about two
tests.
